subject: Television & Streaming
title: The DVR Changed the Rules
description: One-minute skill: The DVR Changed the Rules.

hook.text: TiVo launched in 1999 and terrified TV executives. For the first time, viewers could skip commercials.

buildup.text: The DVR let people record shows and watch later. Suddenly, Tuesday at 8 PM didn't matter anymore.

discovery.text: Networks panicked. Their entire business model depended on live viewers watching ads in real time.

twist.text: Instead of killing TV, DVRs made people watch more of it. Time-shifting meant fitting more shows into a week.

climax.text: The DVR proved that viewers wanted control over when they watched—a lesson streaming would take even further.

punchline.text: The remote gave us channels. The DVR gave us time.

quiz.question: Why did TiVo terrify television executives?
